title: Self-supervised imaging search identifies 16 spectroscopically confirmed quasars at z≈5.94–6.45
summary: Contrastive learning on DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, followed by SED-fit prioritization, selected sources for spectroscopy; follow-up confirmed 16 quasars at z=5.94–6.45. Several show uncommon narrow Lyα lines, strong Lyα+N V equivalent widths or mildly red observed-frame NIR slopes, and three lie in regions traditional color cuts would miss. The 16-object reported sample includes 15 new literature discoveries and one independently confirmed DESI DR1 source; the 45% follow-up yield includes previously known quasars among 40 observed targets.
ai_technology: Self-supervised contrastive-learning neural network applied to DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, with SED-fit prioritization
organization: Max Planck Institute for Astronomy; Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile; Jet Propulsion Laboratory; Universidad Diego Portales; University of Geneva; collaborators

evidence.tested: Contrastive learning on DESI Legacy Survey DR10 multiband images, followed by SED-fit prioritization, selected sources for spectroscopy; follow-up confirmed 16 quasars at z=5.94–6.45.
evidence.unknown: Only 40 candidates were followed up from 1,139 high-priority candidates, so the reported 45% follow-up yield is not completeness or precision over the full sample. That yield counts 18 quasars among 40 targets, including previously known recoveries. The publisher abstract calls all 16 new; the paper body distinguishes 15 new literature discoveries and one additional candidate independently confirmed in DESI DR1 but not reported in literature at the time. Do not overstate population completeness.
evidence.ai_role: Learned an image embedding where candidate quasars formed overdensities, allowing atypical sources beyond standard color selection to be prioritized for spectroscopic validation. Spectroscopy confirmed the quasars; AI did not determine their redshifts alone.
